title: Hatshepsut's obelisk inscription dedicating it to her father Amun

tellings.quote: and I've read the translated hieroglyphs and she said she said um she said [clears throat] as for this obelisk it's something I'm paraphrasing but it's like as for this obelisk I erected this uh from um from electrum

plain: An inscription on the obelisk of Hatshepsut, an ancient Egyptian queen who ruled as pharaoh, at the temple of Karnak dedicates the tall stone pillar to her father, the god Amun, and says she raised it using electrum, a natural mix of gold and silver. The researcher Luke Caverns says he has read the translated hieroglyphs and paraphrases them: "as for this obelisk I erected this from electrum." He raises it as a clue that the monument was once covered in precious metal.
